questions.question: Which among the following methods do most Indian households use for obtaining safe drinking water?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Boiling**__.

__
 
• **Boiling**

 
 
• **​**Boiling is one of the **oldest methods for getting safe drinking water** and it is a **widely practised household water treatment** method used for water purification.
 
• The main purpose of boiling water is **to kill germs** that are present in it.
 
• When water is boiled, it helps remove microorganisms that cannot withstand high temperatures.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Freezing**

 
 
• **​**Freezing is the process in which something changes from liquid to solid as the temperature becomes lower.
 
 
 
• **Storing**
 
 
• **​**Storing means to put aside or accumulate for use when needed, to put for safekeeping, to place or leave in a location.
 
 
 
• **Recycling**
 
 
• **​**Recycling is the process of converting waste materials into new materials and objects.

questions.question: Which of the following agreements between India and Pakistan is also known as the 'Nehru-Liaquat Agreement'?

options.text: Agreement between India and Pakistan regarding resumption of rail traffic
Agreement between India and Pakistan regarding security and rights of minorities
Agreement between India and Pakistan relating to air services
Agreement for avoidance of double taxation between India and Pakistan

questions.solution:

__
 
• **Nehru-Liaquat Agreement**

 
 
• **​**The Nehru–Liaquat Pact, also known as the Delhi Pact, was **a bilateral agreement between India and Pakistan**.
 
• To provide **a framework for the treatment of minorities** in both countries.
 
• It was signed in 1950 in Delhi by former Prime Minister Nehru and former Prime Minister of Pakistan Liaquat Ali Khan.
 
• According to the agreement, India and Pakistan will be accountable to each other for the treatment of minorities in their countries.

• **​**Refugees were allowed to return undisturbed to dispose of their property.
 
• Abducted women and looted property had to be returned.
 
• Forced conversions were unrecognized.

questions.question: What is NOT true about the livestock sector as per the Economic Survey of India 2020?

questions.solution:

• The livestock sector is related to the **management and care of animals** in which the genetic qualities are further developed for profit.
 
• It grew at a Compound Annual Growth Rate (CAGR) of** 8.24 per cent** during **2014-15 to 2018-19.**
 
• Its contribution to total agriculture and allied sector GVA has increased from **24.32 per cent to 28.63 per cen**t in the last five years.
 
• It has been assumed to help in **achieving the goal of doubling farmers’ income**.
 
• It has become the **secondary source of income** for millions of rural families.
 
• As of now, **it doesn't have the potential to replace the agriculture sector as India's most rural population is dependent on it**.

questions.question: What is the shallowest part of an ocean showing an average gradient of 1° or even less called?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Continental shelf**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Continental shelf **

 
 
• **​The **Continental shelf is a relatively shallow sea and extended part of each continent occupied by the bay.
 
• It is the shallowest part of the ocean showing an** average gradient of 1° or even less**.
 
• The shelf usually ends at a very vertical slope, which is called a **shelf brake.**
 
• The width of the continental shelves varies from one ocean to another.
 
• The average width of continental shelves is about **80 km.**
 
• The shelves are almost absent or very narrow along some of the margins like the coasts of Chile, the west coast of Sumatra, etc.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Oceanic trench**

 
 
• **​**Ocean trenches are **long, narrow depressions on the seafloor**.
 
• These chasms are the deepest parts of the ocean and some of the deepest natural spots on Earth.
 
 
 
• **Continental slope**
 
 
• **​**A continental slope is a slope between the outer edge of the continental shelf and the deep ocean floor.

questions.question: How much water carried by the Indus river system can India use under the Indus water treaty (1960)?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**20%**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• **Indus water treaty (1960)**

 
 
• **​**The Indus Water Treaty is a water-distribution treaty **signed between India and Pakistan on 19 September 1960**.
 
• The treaty was signed by then **Prime Minister Jawaharlal Nehru and the President of Pakistan, Ayub Khan**.
 
• It was brokered by the **World Bank**.
 
• The treaty gives **India 20%** of the water from the Indus river system and the rest **80% to Pakistan**.
 
• Treaty gives India control over **3 eastern rivers (Beas, Ravi and Sutlej).**
 
• Pakistan gets control of **3 western rivers (Chenab, Indus and Jhelum)**.
 
• The treaty allows India to use the waters of the western rivers for **limited irrigation use** and **non-consumable use** for applications like **power generation, navigation etc.**
